# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would become applicable (high confidence). However, following a "Digital Omnibus on AI" amendment agreed by the Parliament and Council and entered into force on 27 July 2026, the applicable date for Annex III obligations has been extended to **2 December 2027**, while obligations for high-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I now apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence). Some sources continue to cite the original 2026 date, apparently without accounting for this extension, and a small number of lower-confidence claims suggest even later or different dates, creating residual uncertainty.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
As originally adopted under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the AI Act provided that Annex III high-risk obligations would apply 24 months after entry into force, i.e. on 2 August 2026 (high confidence) [EU AI Act: first regulation on artificial intelligence](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline) [EU AI Act Timeline: Key Dates For Compliance](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline).

### The Digital Omnibus Amendment
The European Parliament and Council reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 on a "Digital Omnibus on AI" that would adjust the application timeline for high-risk AI rules (high confidence) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). One EU source states the Omnibus was "adopted on 19 November 2025, with political agreement reached 7 May 2026," and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). **This chronology is internally inconsistent**, since an adoption date (19 November 2025) cannot precede the political agreement it purportedly finalizes (7 May 2026); readers should treat the specific adoption date in this claim with caution pending clarification from an authoritative Official Journal citation, even though the medium-confidence score reflects the source's otherwise high authority. One low-confidence source identifies the amending act as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, though this citation is not corroborated by official sources [EU AI Act Annex III Deadline 2027](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027) [EU AI Act timeline and planning dates](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html).

### Current Applicable Dates
Following the Omnibus's entry into force, Annex III high-risk AI obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), according to multiple EU guidance sources [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) [Timeline for the Implementation of the EU AI Act](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems classified as such because they are embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) [Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). Under Article 113(c)(i) of the consolidated text, Chapter III Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III systems), excluding Article 6(5), apply from this 2 December 2027 date (low confidence, single source) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113).

### Legacy Systems and Transitional Rules
Article 111(2) provides that the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems already on the market or in service before the Chapter III application date only if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward (high confidence) [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727). However, an EU guidance page describing this same rule references the date explicitly as 2 August 2026 rather than the Omnibus-extended date, suggesting inconsistent updating across official sources (medium confidence) [Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111).

### Analyst Interpretation
Some analysts characterize 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as "backstop dates" that would have applied automatically absent further amendment, implying ongoing legislative uncertainty (low confidence) [LinkedIn commentary](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several news/legal-analysis sources still describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, likely predating or unaware of the Omnibus extension (low confidence) [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance). One unreliable, uncorroborated news blog claims a further delay to 2 August 2029, asserting a "final text agreed in September 2026" that pushed back the date because harmonised standards and notified bodies were not ready; this rationale is plausible in form but contradicts official EU guidance and lacks any corroborating source, so it is flagged as unsupported (low confidence) [AI Omnibus delay claim](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update). One source states the Annex I deadline is 2 August 2027 rather than 2028, contradicting the majority view (low confidence, flagged) [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act). As noted above, the EU's own digital-strategy page gives an internally contradictory adoption/agreement chronology for the Omnibus and should be treated cautiously (medium confidence, flagged) [Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). The EUR-Lex consolidated text and Article 111 guidance also appear internally inconsistent regarding which date governs legacy system obligations.

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise, confirmed Official Journal citation for the Omnibus amending act remains unclear, including its correct adoption date. It is unresolved whether the 2029 delay claim has any legislative basis despite its stated rationale about unready standards and notified bodies. It is unclear whether Article 111(2)'s reference date has been formally updated post-Omnibus, and whether conditions tied to harmonised standards or notified body readiness could further shift the 2027/2028 dates.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
As originally adopted, the EU AI Act set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III would become applicable (high confidence). However, following a "Digital Omnibus on AI" amendment agreed by the Parliament and Council and entered into force on 27 July 2026, the applicable date for Annex III obligations has been extended to **2 December 2027**, while obligations for high-risk systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I now apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence). Some sources continue to cite the original 2026 date, apparently without accounting for this extension, and a small number of lower-confidence claims suggest even later or different dates, creating residual uncertainty.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
As originally adopted under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, the AI Act provided that Annex III high-risk obligations would apply 24 months after entry into force, i.e. on 2 August 2026 (high confidence) [EU AI Act: first regulation on artificial intelligence](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence) [Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline) [EU AI Act Timeline: Key Dates For Compliance](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline).

### The Digital Omnibus Amendment
The European Parliament and Council reached political agreement on 7 May 2026 on a "Digital Omnibus on AI" that would adjust the application timeline for high-risk AI rules (high confidence) [Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules). The Omnibus was adopted on 19 November 2025, with political agreement reached 7 May 2026, and entered into force on 27 July 2026 (medium confidence) [Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). One low-confidence source identifies the amending act as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, though this citation is not corroborated by official sources [EU AI Act Annex III Deadline 2027](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027) [EU AI Act timeline and planning dates](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html).

### Current Applicable Dates
Following the Omnibus's entry into force, Annex III high-risk AI obligations now apply from **2 December 2027** (high confidence), according to multiple EU guidance sources [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) [Timeline for the Implementation of the EU AI Act](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems classified as such because they are embedded in regulated products under Annex I apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation) [Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai). Under Article 113(c)(i) of the consolidated text, Chapter III Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III systems), excluding Article 6(5), apply from this 2 December 2027 date (low confidence, single source) [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113).

### Legacy Systems and Transitional Rules
Article 111(2) provides that the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems already on the market or in service before the Chapter III application date only if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward (high confidence) [EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727). However, an EU guidance page describing this same rule references the date explicitly as 2 August 2026 rather than the Omnibus-extended date, suggesting inconsistent updating across official sources (medium confidence) [Article 111 guidance](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111).

### Analyst Interpretation
Some analysts characterize 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 as "backstop dates" that would have applied automatically absent further amendment, implying ongoing legislative uncertainty (low confidence) [LinkedIn commentary](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several news/legal-analysis sources still describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, likely predating or unaware of the Omnibus extension (low confidence) [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance). One unreliable, uncorroborated news blog claims a further delay to 2 August 2029, which contradicts official EU guidance and lacks support (low confidence, flagged) [AI Omnibus delay claim](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update). One source states the Annex I deadline is 2 August 2027 rather than 2028, contradicting the majority view (low confidence, flagged) [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act). The EUR-Lex consolidated text and Article 111 guidance appear internally inconsistent regarding which date governs legacy system obligations.

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise, confirmed Official Journal citation for the Omnibus amending act remains unclear. It is unresolved whether the 2029 delay claim has any legislative basis. It is unclear whether Article 111(2)'s reference date has been formally updated post-Omnibus, and whether conditions tied to harmonised standards or notified body readiness could further shift the 2027/2028 dates.
